walkthroughs.body_html:
Rural Environments — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Rural Environments brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Rural Environments.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which African region suffers severe desertification?
options: Sahel
Maghreb
Cape
Horn of Africa

mcqs.q: What is the maximum rainfall in hot deserts?
options: 100mm
250mm
500mm

mcqs.q: Why do people move from rural to urban areas in LICs?
options: Burgess is for American cities and Hoyt is for European cities.
Because cities in poor countries are always better than the countryside.
Because the government forces them to move to cities.
A combination of push factors (rural poverty, lack of services, agricultural change) and pull factors (perceived jobs, education, healthcare) — though reality often disappoints.

mcqs.q: Why do earthquakes typically cause more deaths in LICs than HICs?
options: Burgess is for American cities and Hoyt is for European cities.
HICs never have earthquake deaths because of advanced technology.
LICs often have poorly enforced building codes, weak emergency response, dense informal housing and limited preparedness — not because the earthquakes are stronger.
LICs have more earthquake deaths because more earthquakes happen there.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the Burgess and Hoyt urban land use models?
options: Because the government forces them to move to cities.
Burgess (1925) describes concentric rings radiating from the CBD; Hoyt (1939) describes sectors (wedges) extending along transport routes — recognising how transport shapes urban growth.
Burgess and Hoyt models show the same thing in different drawings.
Burgess is for American cities and Hoyt is for European cities.
